run.head: d1a78f7
run.mode: author's own gate on the fix for rounds 4 through 6, plus the outcome of one agnostic review and one incomplete review
gaps: Round 3 of the agnostic review died mid-step-5 on a stream disconnect and never wrote a report. It confirmed the line-continuation finding before dying; what else it would have raised is unknown
No completed agnostic review exists for this head. The two commits after the round-3 review, and the message-only rewrite, are ungated by an external reviewer

deterministic.reason: em dashes only; portless inverts that half of the gate. Zero ' -- ' in added lines
detector renamed to isUnsafeToAppendArgs, zero hits for the old name
one untouched line in cli-utils.ts, the npm '--' forwarding comment, accurate and unaffected
cli.ts:1456, the defect, is gone from the list. Six remaining hits: the spawn itself, the resolver's own two sites, a diagnostic message, and two usesPortless checks that answer a different question

'(' , backtick and '$(' uncovered. The resolver already declines those scripts because their first token is not a framework name, so a guard clause would be unreachable; a regression test pins the outcome instead
self-inflicted: the message-only rewrite retired every sha the earlier reports name. This report closes it for d1a78f7

findings_fixed.claim: Expo package scripts receive HOST=127.0.0.1 in LAN mode, breaking Metro HMR
findings_fixed.verification: built CLI, real bun, LAN marker set: plain expo script and one ending in a comment both report HOST unset

findings_fixed.claim: A shell comment makes the injected --port/--host disappear
findings_fixed.verification: child argv observed as ['dev'] under bun and npm; guard now rejects a word-initial '#'

findings_fixed.claim: Docs overstate support for env-prefixed and wrapped scripts
findings_fixed.verification: five surfaces now name five skip classes, enumerated from the early returns rather than from the reports

findings_fixed.claim: Framework discovery coupled to append safety, so the carve-out goes blind for any declined script
findings_fixed.verification: resolveFrameworkBasename returns 'expo' for four declined shapes; the test that pinned the conflation was replaced

findings_fixed.claim: An escaped space before '#' misread as a comment, a regression against 1aba57e
findings_fixed.verification: word start tracked as state; '--open /foo\ #bar' injects again

findings_fixed.claim: The corrected scope limit still omitted runner flags before the script name
findings_fixed.verification: fifth class documented on all five surfaces

findings_fixed.claim: A comment after a line continuation still opens a comment
findings_fixed.verification: reproduced against real bun before fixing; test red without it

findings_fixed.claim: '&>' is a bash extension; dash backgrounds the command and loses every appended flag
findings_fixed.verification: same line run under bash and dash side by side, then the whole corpus under /bin/dash: one violation before, zero after

harness_findings.claim: The differential sweep defaulted to bun and neither CI job installs it, so the file skipped on both runners
harness_findings.note: found by running it under a PATH that mimics CI, not by reading the workflow

harness_findings.claim: The shim helper forced PATH=/usr/bin:/bin, leaving the Windows child without System32 so the .cmd shim never ran
harness_findings.note: six tests, red since 13c2c38, the branch's first commit. ci-windows now passes for the first time in the PR

method_errors.claim: Six Windows failures reported as pre-existing baseline
method_errors.reality: they arrived in 13c2c38, the branch's first commit. The comparison was against 1aba57e, also on this branch, instead of the merge base
method_errors.closed_by: a pre-existing claim is only pre-existing against origin/main; recorded in the conventions ledger

method_errors.claim: A subshell guard clause was added alongside the '#' fix
method_errors.reality: force-red showed the test passed before the fix too: the resolver already declines those scripts, so the clause was unreachable

issue_candidates.title: A subshell or leading command substitution hides the framework from the resolver
issue_candidates.evidence: verified on the built CLI: '(expo start --port 4567)' and '`printf expo` start --port 4567' both export HOST=127.0.0.1 in LAN mode
issue_candidates.why_out_of_scope: closing it requires parsing shell syntax, larger than this PR

issue_candidates.title: cli.test.ts is not hermetic against the worktree branch prefix
issue_candidates.evidence: six tests fail locally when the branch name leaks into expected hostnames; CI never sees it
issue_candidates.why_out_of_scope: pre-existing against main, verified this time

issue_candidates.title: Injection is skipped for scripts where appending would be safe
issue_candidates.evidence: env prefix, exec, time, and leading substitution all resolve to no injection though the shell would accept the flags
issue_candidates.why_out_of_scope: over-conservatism, documented as a scope limit; widening it is a feature decision for the maintainer

note: The durable artifact of this round is not the fixes, it is the corpus. Five rounds hardened one guard by imagination and each shipped with the next cell open; the corpus found the sixth on a shell the author's machine does not have, in CI, before a maintainer saw it. Promoted to the catalog as substrate differential corpus.
